newsitem.title: UK: Two Palestinians found guilty of London bombings.
newsitem.headline: Two Palestinians found guilty of London bombings.

text.p: Two Palestinians were convicted at Britain's Old Bailey Criminal Court on Wednesday of plotting bomb attacks against Jewish targets in London, one of which badly damaged the Israeli embassy in 1994.
Jawad Botmeh and Samar Alami were to be sentenced on Monday. The judge released a third man, Mahmoud Abu-Wardeh, clearing him of all charges.

They were accused of conspiring to plant two bombs -- one outside the Israeli Embassy and one near a Jewish charity in north London, causing millions of pounds (dollars) worth of damage, in what prosecutors said was an attempt to sabotage the Middle East peace process.
"Mercifully no one was killed or seriously injured but they were grave acts of terrorism," the judge, Justice Patrick Garland, told the jury in summing up the two-month trial.

Botmeh, 28, and his female partner Alami, 30, hoped to damage the Middle East peace process and "paint the name of Palestine on the mountain -- to be seen at the four corners of the earth", prosecutor David Calvert-Smith said.
He had told the court the two were part of a Palestinian guerrilla cell in Britain. "They have drawn their inspiration from the PFLP (Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine)," he said.
Police traced the pair after finding a cache of arms and bomb ingredients in a safe deposit box. Evidence linked Botmeh and Salami to it.
The three defendants had all denied the charges.

Calvert-Smith said a third bomber may never be brought to justice. He said Botmeh and Alami had enlisted the services of "a respectable middle-aged woman" to plant the bomb outside the Israeli embassy, which neighbours Kensington Palace, in June 1994.
In November another Palestinian woman, 49-year-old Nadia Zekra, was freed when the judge said there was not enough evidence against her.

The embassy bomb was set off after then-Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin and King Hussein of Jordan signed the Washington Declaration which paved the way for peace between their two countries, Garland said.
